title: Frozen Evaluation Recommendation-Episode Lifecycle and Grouping Contract

snapshot_specification.rule: Evaluation recommendation episodes are evaluated on the official evening 20:30 America/New_York decision snapshot.

start_rule.definition: An episode opens on the first official 20:30 snapshot where an immutable security is surfaced by a candidate system (assigned to Enter Now, Armed, or Qualified Waitlist) after not currently having an active evaluation recommendation episode for that system.
start_rule.cardinality: At most one active evaluation recommendation episode is permitted per immutable security per candidate system at any snapshot. Tracking and reset state are independently maintained per immutable security.

continuation_rule.definition: An active episode continues across consecutive official 20:30 snapshots while the security remains continuously surfaced (in any qualifying state: Enter Now, Armed, or Qualified Waitlist).
continuation_rule.state_transitions: Transitions between visible surfaced states (e.g. Enter Now -> Armed, Armed -> Enter Now, Armed -> Qualified Waitlist) do NOT by themselves create a new evaluation episode. Contiguous surfaced observations remain grouped within the same single active episode.

close_rule.definition: An active episode closes on the earliest occurrence of any of the following terminal conditions:

triggers.description: First official 20:30 snapshot where the security is no longer surfaced (downgraded to Hidden / not surfaced / disqualified).
Episode reaches exactly 21 trading sessions from episode start date.
Explicit recommendation invalidation under a later frozen state/entry contract.

anti_double_count_rule.definition: If the 21-session maximum cap is reached while the security remains continuously surfaced by the candidate system, the episode closes with close_reason 'max_session_cap_reached' and a new episode is NOT automatically opened on the next trading session.
anti_double_count_rule.eligibility_reset: The security becomes eligible to initiate a new evaluation recommendation episode only after at least one official 20:30 snapshot in which it is NOT surfaced (i.e. a hidden / unsurfaced snapshot must occur before a subsequent surfacing can open a new episode). Suppression and eligibility are tracked independently per immutable security.
anti_double_count_rule.purpose: Prevents one persistent signal or permanently qualifying security from inflating sample counts or being counted as repeated independent recommendations.

future_entry_plan_rule.definition: Once LONG-002F introduces frozen entry-plan IDs, a material change to a frozen entry plan, trigger, or invalidation closes the prior recommendation ID and creates a new operational recommendation ID. However, this later operational rule must not retroactively alter the LONG-002E evaluation recommendation-episode grouping without an explicit amendment.

outcome_semantics.definition: The primary evaluation recommendation-episode outcome is strictly frozen to the episode-start 20:30 observation and its existing primary Stage C label/reference-entry semantics.
outcome_semantics.prohibition_of_post_start_pooling: clean_target_reached_10_10 and time_to_target_if_reached are measured from the episode-start observation/reference entry only. They must NEVER be computed as a logical OR, maximum, or composite across subsequent constituent snapshots within the episode.
outcome_semantics.rationale: Freezing the outcome to the episode-start observation prevents favorable post-start rows or delayed market moves from retroactively determining episode success, eliminating selection and lookahead degrees of freedom for Stage E.

prediction_fields_semantics.primary_prediction_rule: Primary start-of-episode performance, ranking, decile lift, and calibration evaluations must use the prediction fields from the episode-start 20:30 observation (start_score_or_probability and start_rank).
prediction_fields_semantics.descriptive_fields_restriction: max_score_or_probability and best_rank are strictly descriptive trajectory diagnostics across the episode duration and are explicitly PROHIBITED from primary start-of-episode performance, ranking, or calibration calculations.

conceptual_distinctions.stage_c_master_opportunity_episodes: Stage C master opportunity episodes are ex-post ground-truth labeling windows (up to 21 sessions following the first anchor entry that reaches at least +10%) that group natural market outcome phenomena. Evaluation recommendation episodes are candidate-system-generated evaluation grouping units that reflect when a specific model chose to surface a security.
conceptual_distinctions.live_order_lifecycles: Evaluation recommendation episodes do not represent live brokerage orders, broker-fill executions, or position lifecycles.
conceptual_distinctions.brokerage_positions: Evaluation recommendation episodes do not represent account positions or portfolio holdings.

denominator_and_reporting_rules.dual_reporting_mandatory: LONG-002E model evaluation must report BOTH raw observation-level diagnostics AND unique evaluation recommendation-episode metrics.
denominator_and_reporting_rules.raw_daily_rows_prohibition: Raw daily observation rows must NOT be treated as independent recommendations or used as the denominator for product-usefulness claims.
denominator_and_reporting_rules.primary_sample_interpretation: Primary sample counts and product-usefulness metrics must evaluate unique evaluation recommendation episodes alongside independent master opportunity episodes, distinct tickers, calendar coverage, and year/sector concentration.
